newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Tuesday despite some profit taking, on their highest volume in three years, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.83 percent, or 2.34 points, to 282.87 on heavy all-share turnover of 266 million shekels against 220 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.58 percent higher at 289.76.
"The positive trend is continuing and volume is very high. The rise of Israeli shares traded in New York also helped the market today," said Michael Weiss of Evergreen Capital Markets.
Weiss said fresh money was coming into the market from investors increasing the equity weighting in their portfolios and from the mutual funds.
"The market is very selective, which shows that the main players in the market are sophisticated investors. The general public is still outside," he said.

"The market is very strong and continues to rise despite some profit taking. We might see a light correction but the positive trend will continue and this is the time to buy shares," said Danniella Finn of Batucha Securities and Investments.

Weiss added that the rise in bond prices and expectations for declining interest rates were also adding to the positive mood. "As bond yields decline the stock market becomes more attractive," he said.
"The market is becoming more selective but activity continues to be strong. If there is no political disaster the positive trend will continue," Finn added.
Nice Systems rose 3.0 percent to 10,527 agorot. Lehman Brothers said on Tuesday it was raising its 12-month price target for Nice to $40 from $30.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which closed unchanged at 540 agorot on volume of 29.1 million shekels; Koor Industries, which rose 3.25 percent to 31,248 agorot on turnover of nine million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 3.0 percent to 21,385 agorot on volume of 7.7 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
